intro.data: Pairing is powerful: pair a thing with itself and you get a duplicator. Build the Diagonal that turns one value into a pair of identical copies — projecting either side gives the original back.
intro.alchemy: Pairing is powerful: pair a thing with itself and you get a duplicator. Build the Diagonal that turns one material into a pair of identical copies — projecting either side gives the original back.
intro.spellcraft: Pairing is powerful: pair a thing with itself and you get a duplicator. Build the Diagonal that turns one essence into a pair of identical copies — drawing either side gives the original back.
intro.abstract: Pair an object with itself: Δ = ⟨id, id⟩ : A → A×A. Build it, so π₁∘Δ = id_A and π₂∘Δ = id_A.

goal.data: Wire the Name through the Diagonal to produce the pair of copies.
goal.alchemy: Wire the Salt through the Diagonal to produce the pair of copies.
goal.spellcraft: Wire the Light through the Diagonal to produce the pair of copies.
goal.abstract: Wire A through Δ to reach A×A.

afterSuccess.data: The Diagonal is just ⟨id, id⟩ — pairing a thing with itself. Both projections give back the original, so it's a faithful copy. The product's universal property gives you duplication for free.
afterSuccess.alchemy: The Diagonal is just ⟨id, id⟩ — pairing a thing with itself. Both projections give back the original, so it's a faithful copy. The product gives you duplication for free.
afterSuccess.spellcraft: The Diagonal is just ⟨id, id⟩ — pairing a thing with itself. Both draws give back the original, so it's a faithful copy. The product gives you duplication for free.
afterSuccess.abstract: Δ = ⟨id_A, id_A⟩, so π₁∘Δ = π₂∘Δ = id_A. The diagonal copies A into A×A.

reveal.summary: The diagonal Δ : A → A×A pairs an object with itself. Both projections recover the original: π₁ ∘ Δ = π₂ ∘ Δ = id_A.
reveal.moreFormal: The diagonal is a special pairing built from the universal property. It is what lets a category model duplication of data — not every category has it, but any with products does.
reveal.programmerAnalogy: const dup = (x) => [x, x]; both [0] and [1] give x back.
